title: Female borrowers who describe the local cultural or geographic context may fund more slowly.
Mentioning financial urgency may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Mentioning the use of previous loans to sustain a business may slow funding for women.
Mentioning that the loan covers 100% of the price may slow funding for women.
Mentioning the BRAC microfinance program may be an exception to the general rule that institutional names slow funding for women.
Female borrowers who specify their age fund faster.
Mentioning the loan amount in local currency predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Expressing heartfelt thanks for a previously received loan may accelerate funding for women.
Stating the loan amount in local currency may slow funding speed for female borrowers.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Longer pitch text predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their husband's role or family structure fund faster.
Female borrowers who express explicit gratitude in their pitches fund more slowly.
